origins: Many believers were taught to be selfless, to turn the other cheek, and to put others first. Those are good teachings, but they can be bent into the idea that having any limits is sinful. People who grew up caring for a troubled parent or sibling may have been told that their needs did not matter.
teaches: Jesus “frequently withdrew to the wilderness to pray,” and He did not heal everyone in every town. Proverbs says, “Guard your heart with all diligence, for from it flow springs of life,” and “Like a city whose walls are broken down is a man who does not control his temper.” Paul writes, “Each one should carry his own load.” Jesus said the second greatest commandment is to love your neighbor as yourself, which assumes some care for yourself. Boundaries are not walls to keep love out. They are fences that protect what is valuable, including your ability to love others well.
self_statements: Saying no is putting myself first.
errors: Believing I am either selfless or selfish.
Insisting that I should always be available.
Calling myself selfish for having limits.
Feeling guilty and concluding that boundaries are wrong.
questions: Where did I learn that limits are selfish?
Did Jesus ever step away or say no?
What happens to my love and patience when I have no limits?
What is the difference between selfish and healthy?
What boundary would help me love better?
Who would benefit if I were rested and well?
truth: Boundaries are a way to steward my time, energy, and heart so I can love well. Jesus Himself withdrew to rest and pray. Healthy limits are not selfish. They help me serve without resentment.
hw_truths: I am to guard my heart.
log: Each week, record a boundary you kept and what it allowed.
actions: Explain it simply, without a long defense.
Take time alone like Jesus did.
prayer: Lord Jesus, You withdrew to be with the Father. Teach me to guard my heart, set loving limits, and serve without resentment. Amen.
hw_questions: Where did I learn limits are selfish?
name_example: Sarah can write: “Jesus withdrew to pray, so I can set healthy limits.”
meta: Christian belief counseling for “Setting boundaries is selfish.” with BSB scriptures, questions, songs, and practical homework.
